day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Alright, alright, give us a sec. Anyone hurt?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah, pretty much. Don't think about it too much right now, keep moving. Are you hurt anywhere?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Fair enough, take a minute. But we're going to need you when you're ready.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Yeah, constantly. But three days of first aid and two bottles of water isn't going to cut it, so heavy or not we need to get moving. What else have we got?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Right, so water first. Are we in a forest, near a river, anything like that? Because if we can find running water we're sorted on that front. Shelter and signal we can work on once we're not dying of thirst.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Two blankets, four people. Mikey gets one, he's been in shock most of the day. The other one we share between the three of us, wrap it round all of us near the fire. Body heat's more efficient anyway.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci's better at keeping things together back here, and I'd rather be doing something useful than sitting around. Two hours each way though, that's most of the day gone - we need to think about whether we're carrying enough to make it worth the trip or setting up some kind of relay.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Hang on, you said I was going with you to the water source two seconds ago, now you're handling it? Which is it? I'm happy either way but let's not have two of us heading off in different directions with no plan. I'll take the first aid kit, DaVinci can sort the camp patches.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: No, I haven't. But hang on, that empty bottle next to the rationing plan is a bit more pressing right now - did you put that there?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Right, so that's twice now. The bottle and now crackers. I like Donatello, she's kept us alive this far, but we can't have people going off-script on the rationing plan she literally wrote herself. That's a bit rich isn't it. 

We need to bring it up, all of us together, no drama, just lay it out. She's rational, she responds to logic - so we present the facts, no accusations, just "this was found, this was seen, what's going on." If there's a reason, fine, let's hear it. But if we let this slide it falls apart for everyone.

You up for having that conversation when she gets back?

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: Honestly? Yeah, probably. What's the actual risk if we leave it tonight - is anything going to come down on us or is it just not ideal? If it's fine until morning then fine, but I don't want to find out at 3am that the answer was "no actually it wasn't fine."

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Probably, but that's not really the problem right now is it. We've got one patch, two leaks - food or Mikey. Food, yeah? We can't eat soggy rations and Mikey can move, the food can't. Mikey, grab your blanket and shift over to this side, you're bunking near the fire tonight.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah we're on the same page then, food it is. Let's get it done.
Don't be daft, it's fine. You alright? Bad dream?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Nah, it's not a waste of time. Signal's one of our three priorities remember, Donatello said it herself. The flowers are maybe a bit much but honestly if it keeps your spirits up while you're doing something useful then crack on. Bigger the better.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Two days to build, risk of capsizing... what's the alternative though? Stay here and hope someone finds us? We've got the SOS on the beach which helps, but we don't know how long that takes. 

Walk me through the capsizing risk - is that a "probably fine if we're careful" risk or a "genuinely likely to kill us all" risk? Because those are very different conversations. And what are we actually building it out of, those metal panels aren't exactly going to float naturally are they, what's keeping us buoyant?

I'm not saying no, I'm saying I want to understand it properly before we commit two days of energy to it. What's your gut on it?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Honestly Mikey, I don't know. Probably more like ourselves than we'd expect, just... turned up a bit. The good and the bad. 

But rescue is coming. We've got a signal on the beach, we've got a raft plan, we're not just sitting here. Try not to let your brain run too far ahead of where we actually are. 

Did you get any sleep at all?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down nearby, not too close, doesn't say anything for a bit*

You don't have to talk. Just didn't want you sitting out here on your own.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Erm... sysadmin by day so usually something involving a computer. Gaming mostly, bit of Kerbal Space Program, that sort of thing. You?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Five hundred meters is doable for a strong swimmer in calm water, but that reef looks like it could cut you to pieces if the current's wrong. And if something goes wrong out there we can't exactly come and get you, can we. 

Why the reef specifically though? What does that get us that the SOS on the beach doesn't? Because if you've got a solid reason I'm listening, but if it's just... needing to do something, I get that, but there might be a better way to scratch that itch that doesn't involve you drowning. 

And why aren't you telling the others?

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Yeah, I know, sorry - I got talking to DaVinci and it slipped. I'll go sort it now.

Bit weird, yeah. I don't love the idea of being logged like I'm a resource to be tracked, but I get why you're doing it. If something goes wrong you want to know what happened and when. Just... maybe give us a heads up next time? Would've felt less like I was being watched if I'd known.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Donatello. Oi. We're all sitting here, first proper downtime we've had since the crash, and you're doing admin. The notebook can wait an hour. Come and sit with us.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Oh that's actually not bad. Mirrors are one of the standard signalling methods aren't they, you can see a reflection from miles away on a clear day. Angle it right and any aircraft or boat on the horizon is going to clock it. 

Worth doing alongside the SOS rather than instead of it though - more signals the better. Donatello, is there anything structurally important about those mirror panels or can we pull one without causing problems?

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: Not really music, I'm more of a reader. Terry Pratchett mostly, if I'm being honest. Could probably do with having a Discworld book right now actually. What made you stop with the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Right, so let's just get it done then. How many of us do you need on it and what exactly needs finishing? If it's a two person job there's no point all four of us standing around it. Tell me what to do and I'll do it.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Come here.

Look, that probably wasn't our only chance. Probably. But even if it was - we've got the mirror signal now, we've got the SOS, we've got the raft nearly done. We're not just waiting to be found, we're actively doing things to get out of here.

I know that hurt. It hurt all of us. Take a minute.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: Where? What are you looking at?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: Signal pile, like I said. Checked it, it's fine. Why, is something missing?

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
That's actually really good news Mikey, why didn't you say that sooner? If they know the flight path and you don't show up, they're going to call it in, that's what families do. That changes things - there's a decent chance someone's already looking in roughly the right area. 

How specific was it, like did you give them waypoints or just "we're flying from A to B"?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Right, so if that's true then we just need to hold on a bit longer. 48 hours is manageable if we're sensible. 

Someone should put a log on that fire though, we're going to need it tonight.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. I know what you mean.

I think most people feel that way if they're honest about it. The dying part you can sort of... file away and not look at. But the idea of just being gone, like you were never really here - that's the one that actually gets you isn't it.

You've got people who know your flight path. People who were worth telling. That's not nothing Mikey.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: Nah, you kept us alive. That counts for a lot more than easy to be around.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: Right, are we just going to leave it like this then? Three hours and we're out of here, let's at least not leave a complete tip. DaVinci, you're packing anyway, can you consolidate what we're taking versus what we're leaving? Donatello, anything in that notebook we need to hand over to rescue when they arrive - medical stuff, timeline of events? Mikey, you can keep watching the sky, just maybe do it while you're picking up around you.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response: I know. And if we'd hit day five or six and things had gone badly I'd probably have been glad you did. But we didn't get there, and it's all still here, so... maybe just put it in the pile with everything else and we don't need to make a big thing of it.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd have pushed back on the rationing thing earlier. Not in a confrontational way, just... got everyone bought in properly from the start so there was no ambiguity about what the rules were and who they applied to. Including you.

And I'd have let Mikey talk more. I kept trying to move him past the feeling and onto the next task. Probably wasn't what he needed every time.

What are you writing for yourself?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: Ha, yeah that sounds about right. First thing I'm doing is finding the nearest pub.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response: None. That's the point isn't it. They didn't need to serve a purpose.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: Yeah. Just give me a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
